# DEVDESK-210 — Terminal focus and blur: suspend the animation and the background reloads

Sources: `docs/ux/bubbletea-v2-improvements.md` §2.1, `.claude/plans/charm-v2-impact.md` §2 and §4 F2,
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md` ("The broadcast, and the animation tick", "One tick, one chain"),
`docs/architecture/agent-usage.md` ("Live updates (DEVDESK-45)").
API checked in the module cache (`charm.land/bubbletea/v2@v2.1.1`): `tea.View.ReportFocus` (tea.go:184),
`tea.FocusMsg{}` / `tea.BlurMsg{}` (focus.go), mode 1004 set on renderer start and reset on close
(cursed_renderer.go:143/214/381). `bubbles/v2@v2.2.1` `cursor.Model` reacts to raw `tea.FocusMsg`/`tea.BlurMsg`;
`textinput.Update` ignores everything while the input is not focused.

## Blocking questions

**Q1 — A terminal that is visible but not focused (blocks steps 3 and 4, not 1 and 2).**
tmux panes side by side (`focus-events on`) or a second monitor: DevDesk is visible while the user types
elsewhere. That is exactly how `:agent-usage` live updates (DEVDESK-45) are used — watching a Claude Code
session run in another pane. With the story as written, `:agent-usage` reads nothing for as long as the
user works in the other pane, and a footer spinner of a running job freezes on one frame.
- A. As written: blur suspends blink and reloads. Simple; the `:agent-usage` "watch from the side" use case
  shows `paused (terminal not focused)` most of the time.
- B. Blur suspends the blink only; reloads keep running. Most of the battery/CPU gain is lost (reloads are
  the I/O), the visual calm stays.
- C. **(recommended)** A, plus a per-context setting `app.when_unfocused: pause | run` (default `pause`,
  the story's behaviour), editable in `:cfg` > Appearance. `run` restores today's behaviour entirely
  (blink included). It costs one config key, one `:cfg` field and one router predicate (step 6, S).
- D. Suspend reloads only after a grace period (e.g. 2 min without focus). Does not solve the side-pane
  case, adds a timer.

**Q2 — Which periodic reloads are in scope (does not block steps 1 to 5).** The story names `:agent-usage`,
container stats and ports. Others exist:

| Chain | Cadence | Cost | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| dashboard host sample (`HostTickMsg`) | 1 s | `/proc` read | include (step 7) |
| dashboard docker stats (`DockerTickMsg`) | 5 s | `docker stats`, ~2 s each — the most expensive, and the default landing view | include (step 7) |
| dashboard slow round (`RefreshTickMsg`) | ≥ 30 s | `docker system df`, `du` | include (step 7) |
| OCI resources (`oci_resources.RefreshTickMsg`) | 10 s | `docker images` | include (step 7) |
| status monitors (`status` TickMsg) | 1 s countdown + checks | HTTP/ICMP/DNS | **exclude**: monitoring is the point |
| viewer follow (`followTickMsg`) | user toggle `F` | file/log re-read | exclude: explicit user request |
| netdiag forwards tab (`forwardTickMsg`) | 2 s | in-process | exclude: no I/O |

Recommendation: ship steps 1–5 for the three named chains; step 7 (same pattern, S) for dashboard + OCI if
the user agrees.

## Hypotheses (prudent defaults, flag in the PR)

- **H1 — Unknown means focused.** The router starts focused; only a `tea.BlurMsg` suspends anything. A
  `tea.FocusMsg` with no prior blur changes nothing (no Cmd, no message to any view).
- **H2 — A key or a paste proves focus.** A `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.PasteMsg` received while blurred is
  handled as a `FocusMsg` first, then dispatched normally. Self-healing when a FocusIn is lost (tmux pane
  switch, terminal hand-off by `teaexec`, where Bubble Tea's input reader is stopped and the terminal does
  not re-report focus when mode 1004 is set again).
- **H3 — `:agent-usage` header.** `paused (terminal not focused)` whenever the agents level has an open
  aggregate and the terminal is blurred, whether or not the session was already settled (nothing is read
  while blurred, so "paused" is true either way; the reason shown is the one that resumes on focus).
- **H4 — Off-screen views are not told on the edges.** Only the view on screen has a live periodic chain
  (containers and ports chains die off screen because their ticks reach the view on screen, which drops
  them; `:agent-usage` is stopped by `Leave`). A view entering the screen is told the current state
  (level), never asked to refresh: its own `Init` does that.
- **H5 — Footer messages are not frozen.** A footer error set during the blur still expires after 3 s
  (`FooterMessage` timer). The durable trace of a failure is the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`: ⊗ on
  the row, footer detail from `DescribeRow`, `:jobs`). AC4 is about that memory; holding footer timers
  during blur would be a separate UX story.
- **H6 — Not covered, residual:** the text-input cursor blink (`bubbles/cursor`, its own chain, only while
  a field is in edit mode) and a view's own loading spinner (only while its load is in flight) keep running
  during the blur. The router does not forward raw `tea.FocusMsg`/`tea.BlurMsg` to views: `cursor.Focus()`
  on a raw focus would restart blink on cursors the view never meant to show.

## Non-functional requirements

- **CPU / battery:** blurred and idle, the router emits no `animationTickMsg`; the three named views do no
  I/O. Residual wake-ups: one 2 s timer per suspended view (containers, ports) with no I/O and no change to
  render (0 bytes written by the renderer, cf. `TestMeasureRedrawCost`).
- **Correctness:** no job is ever cancelled, paused or delayed by a blur (`jobs.Running()` unaffected);
  registry broadcasts (`ChangedMsg`, failures included) keep reaching every held view.
- **One chain:** after any Blur/Focus sequence, at most one live `animationTickMsg` chain
  (`TestTheRouterHasOneAnimationChain` unchanged and green).
- **Degradation:** a terminal that never sends `BlurMsg` behaves exactly as today (dedicated test).
- **Rules:** 110 (state changes in `Update` only), 126 (no scan on focus), 128 (no footer message on
  focus), 109 (message naming), 201 (case > 5 lines → `handle*`).
- **Guard:** `internal/app/activity_guard_test.go` is not modified. Do not add `tea.Tick` to
  `internal/ui/agentusageview` (the guard counts that package as migrated with no tick of its own); do not
  add `Frame` fields or glyph literals to `netdiag/ports_model.go`.

## Options compared (how views suspend their reloads)

| | A. Router level + views skip I/O (recommended) | B. Views stop their chains, restart on focus | C. Reuse `LeavingView.Leave()` on blur and `Init()` on focus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Router | one bool, read by the cadence; one message to the view on screen | same | calls Leave/Init |
| containers / ports | tick keeps running, the handler skips the fetch; one fetch on focus | needs a generation per chain, otherwise a focus within 2 s of the blur leaves two chains (the containers comment on `PagerExitMsg` already records that bug) | `Init()` starts a **second** `tickCmd` in containers (doubles every refresh) |
| `:agent-usage` | reuses Leave's body and `handleResume` (already generation-based) | same | works, but `Leave` also settles edits (configuration) and may refuse; `Init` reloads whole views |
| Residual wake-ups | one timer per suspended view, no I/O | none | n/a |
| Risk | low | medium (new generations in two views) | high (semantics overloaded) |

**Recommendation: A.** It is the "level, not edge" shape the router already uses for `ensureTick`, keeps
the existing chains intact, and the only new invariant is "a periodic handler checks one flag before I/O".

## ADR draft (to be archived by `archivist` in `docs/backlog.md`)

- **Context:** Bubble Tea v2 reports terminal focus (mode 1004). DevDesk animates and polls in the
  background.
- **Decision:** terminal focus is a router level (`App.terminalBlurred`, zero value = focused). The
  animation cadence reads it: blurred → no chain. Views learn it through `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`
  (to the view on screen on each edge, to a view entering the screen as a level). A periodic chain keeps
  its timer and skips its I/O while blurred; `:agent-usage` stops its chain like `Leave` and resumes like
  `handleResume`. Focus re-reads once the view on screen, never scans.
- **Consequences:** a terminal without mode 1004 is unchanged; a visible-but-unfocused DevDesk is
  paused (Q1); new periodic chains must honour the flag (documented in `app-shell.md`).

## Interfaces (shared by the steps)

```go
// internal/shared/focus.go (new)
// TerminalFocusMsg tells a view whether the terminal has the focus. The router
// sends it to the view on screen when the focus changes, and to a view entering
// the screen. Focused is the level; Resume is set only on the focus edge, to the
// view on screen: re-read once what was suspended (never a scan, Rule 126).
type TerminalFocusMsg struct {
	Focused bool
	Resume  bool
}

// internal/app/focus.go (new)
func (a *App) handleTerminalBlur() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)
func (a *App) handleTerminalFocus() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)
func (a *App) sendFocusTo(target command.ViewType) tea.Cmd // level, Resume=false
func (a *App) wantedCadence() (time.Duration, bool)        // blurred → (0, false), else cadence(...)
```

`App` gains `terminalBlurred bool` (zero value = focused, H1). `cadence()` keeps its signature (existing
tests untouched); `ensureTick` and `handleAnimationTick` call `a.wantedCadence()` instead.

---

## Step 1 — Router: report focus, suspend the animation chain (S) — *animation only, shippable alone*

**Files:** `internal/app/view.go`, `internal/app/app.go` (field, two `case`s, H2 in `handleKeyMsg` /
`handlePasteMsg` entry or in `update` before dispatch), `internal/app/animation.go` (`wantedCadence`),
`internal/app/focus.go` (new). Tests: `internal/app/focus_test.go` (new), `internal/app/screen_test.go`.

**Behaviour:**
- `App.View()` sets `v.ReportFocus = true` (router only).
- `tea.BlurMsg` → `handleTerminalBlur`: `a.terminalBlurred = true`. Nothing else: the live chain's
  in-flight tick reaches `handleAnimationTick`, `wantedCadence` says no, the chain is not renewed and the
  phase is pinned on (existing "at rest" branch sends the last `FrameMsg`). No seq bump needed.
- `tea.FocusMsg` → `handleTerminalFocus`: if not blurred, return `a, nil` (H1). Otherwise clear the flag;
  the `Update` wrapper's `ensureTick` starts the one chain (or keeps the in-flight one if the blur was
  shorter than a tick).
- While blurred, `ensureTick` returns nil after every message, including `jobs.StartMsg`, transitions
  and `jobsChanged`.
- H2: a key or paste while blurred runs `handleTerminalFocus` first, then the normal dispatch.

**Tests to write first (entry → expected):**
1. `TestAppViewReportsFocus`: `App.View().ReportFocus == true`.
   Extend `TestEveryViewIsAScreenWhoseViewWrapsRender`: every view's `View().ReportFocus == false`.
2. `TestBlurStopsTheBlinkChain`: `blinkRouter(t, true)`, `startBlinkChain`, `Update(tea.BlurMsg{})`,
   then `tickAt(a, …)` with the live seq → returned Cmd yields no `animationTickMsg`; `a.anim.ticking ==
   false`; the view's last `jobs.FrameMsg` has `Blink == true` when the tick fell on an "off" phase.
3. `TestNoChainStartsWhileBlurred`: blurred router, view `wants = true`, then `jobs.Running() > 0`
   (start a run) → `ensureTick()` is nil after each `Update`; recorded intervals (`stubAnimationEvery`)
   unchanged.
4. `TestBlurNeverTouchesRunningJobs` (AC3): run started, blur, advance an item to running then done
   via the router's normal messages → registry `Snapshot()` shows the transitions; no item `skipped`/
   `cancelled`; `Running()` is 1 before the done and 0 after.
5. `TestAFailureDuringBlurIsShownOnFocus` (AC4): blur, an item fails (`Advance(..., failed, ...)` through
   the routed message), focus → the view on screen holds a `jobs.ChangedMsg` whose `Failures` contains
   the `FailureKey{Kind, Target, Context}`; `a.jobs.Failures()` has it.
6. `TestFocusRestartsExactlyOneChain` (AC5): blink view, chain started, blur, in-flight tick handled
   (chain dies), `Update(tea.FocusMsg{})` → exactly one new interval recorded, `anim.seq` +1, a second
   `FocusMsg` records nothing. Variant with a running job → interval is `animationFastInterval`.
   Variant "blur then focus before the in-flight tick lands" → no new chain (ticking still true), the
   in-flight tick renews it: still one chain.
7. `TestNeverBlurredBehavesAsToday` (degradation): same scripted sequence (start blink, ticks at 1000 /
   1500 / 2000 ms, start a run, finish it) on a router that receives a `tea.FocusMsg` (no blur) at the
   start and on one that receives nothing → identical recorded intervals, identical `FrameMsg.Blink`
   series, `FocusMsg` returns nil Cmd.
8. `TestStaticMotionNeverBlinksAcrossFocus` (AC6): `motionConfig("static")`, running job, blur, focus,
   ticks → every `FrameMsg` received has `Blink == true`; a blink-only view gets no chain on focus.
9. `TestAKeyWhileBlurredCountsAsFocus` (H2): blurred, blink view, `testutil.Key("down")` → a chain
   starts; `a.terminalBlurred == false`. Same with `testutil.Paste("x")`.
10. Race: extend `TestTheAnimationChainUnderARealProgram` (or a sibling) — real `tea.Program`,
    `p.Send(tea.BlurMsg{})`, wait 3 intervals, count ticks (0 new), `p.Send(tea.FocusMsg{})` → ticks
    resume. Run under `-race`.

**Done when:** tests above green; `TestTheRouterHasOneAnimationChain`, `motion_test.go`,
`animation_*_test.go` unchanged and green.
`go test ./internal/app -count=1 -run 'Focus|Blur|Animation|Motion|Chain|AppView|EveryViewIsAScreen|Blurred'`
then `go test -race ./internal/app -run 'UnderARealProgram|Focus' -count=1`.

## Step 2 — Router → views: `shared.TerminalFocusMsg` (S) — depends on 1

**Files:** `internal/shared/focus.go` (new), `internal/app/focus.go`, `internal/app/jobs.go`
(`enterView` adds `a.sendFocusTo(target)`), `internal/app/app.go` (`reinitializeViews` sends the level to
the rebuilt view on screen). Tests: `internal/app/focus_test.go`.

**Behaviour:**
- Blur edge → the view on screen receives `TerminalFocusMsg{Focused: false}`.
- Focus edge (after a blur) → the view on screen receives `TerminalFocusMsg{Focused: true, Resume: true}`;
  its Cmd is returned. The router itself starts nothing else: no `Init`, no scan request, no footer.
- `enterView` (covers `switchView`, path picker, selection, `scan_details` ×2) and `reinitializeViews`
  (context switch, config reload) send `TerminalFocusMsg{Focused: !a.terminalBlurred}` — always, so a view
  left while blurred does not keep a stale flag.
- Held views off screen receive nothing on the edges (H4).
- The layout is not re-measured (a focus message never changes a footer height).

**Tests to write first:**
1. `TestBlurTellsOnlyTheViewOnScreen`: two held `fakeView`s; blur → on-screen view received
   `TerminalFocusMsg{false,false}` (`receivedOf`), the other received nothing.
2. `TestFocusAsksTheViewOnScreenToResumeOnce`: blur, focus → on-screen view received exactly one
   `{true,true}`; `inits` unchanged; a second `FocusMsg` sends nothing.
3. `TestFocusWithoutBlurTellsNobody` (degradation): `FocusMsg` on a fresh router → no view received a
   `TerminalFocusMsg`, Cmd nil.
4. `TestAViewEnteringTheScreenIsToldTheFocus`: table — blurred / focused × `switchView`, path picker,
   selection entry → the entering view's last `TerminalFocusMsg` is `{Focused: !blurred, Resume: false}`.
5. `TestAContextSwitchWhileBlurredTellsTheRebuiltView`: blurred, `reinitializeViews()` → the new view on
   screen received `{false,false}`.
6. `TestFocusStartsNoScan` (Rule 126): blur, focus with a real `ws` view on screen (or `:sec`) → running
   the returned Cmd yields no `jobs.StartMsg`; `a.jobs.Snapshot()` length unchanged.

**Done when:** green; `go test ./internal/app ./internal/shared -count=1 -run 'Focus|Blur|Entering|Switch'`.

## Step 3 — `:agent-usage`: suspend the poll chain, header hint, resume on focus (M-) — depends on 2; Q1

**Files:** `internal/ui/agentusageview/model.go` (field `unfocused bool`), `update.go` (case
`shared.TerminalFocusMsg` → `handleTerminalFocus`; extract the chain-stopping body of `Leave` into
`func (m Model) stopChain() Model` used by both; `handleResume` and `handlePollTick` return early when
`m.unfocused`), `view.go` (`updatesState`). Tests: `internal/ui/agentusageview/focus_test.go` (new),
reuse helpers from `live_test.go` / `leave_test.go` / `header_live_test.go`.

**Behaviour:**
- `{Focused:false}`: `m.unfocused = true`; at the agents level, `stopChain()` (bump `agentGen`, keep
  `fullPending` when a full read was in flight, clear `reading`/`agentsLoading`). No Cmd.
- `{Focused:true, Resume:true}`: `m.unfocused = false`; return `m.handleResume()` (new generation,
  `pollStopped = false`, silent delta read, or full read with spinner when `fullPending`). At the sessions
  level: nothing (the list is not live).
- `{Focused:true, Resume:false}` (entry): clear the flag only; `Init`'s `resumeCmd` does the read.
- `agentsResumeMsg` or `usagePollTickMsg` while `unfocused`: dropped, no Cmd.
- `updatesState()`: `"paused (terminal not focused)"` when `level == levelAgents && agg != nil &&
  unfocused` (H3); otherwise unchanged (`live` / `paused`).
- No footer message on either edge (Rule 128). No `tea.Tick` added to the package.

**Tests to write first:**
1. Live session open, blur → `GetHeaderInfo` "Updates" value `paused (terminal not focused)`; a
   `usagePollTickMsg` of the previous generation → nil Cmd; a `usageDeltaMsg` of the previous generation
   → dropped, no tick scheduled.
2. Blur then `{true,true}` → header `live`; Cmd runs one `readDeltaCmd` (fixture transcript in
   `t.TempDir()`) answering with the new `agentGen`; no spinner tick in the batch.
3. Settled session (`pollStopped`), blur → header `paused (terminal not focused)`; focus → one read; the
   answer settles it again → header `paused`.
4. Full read in flight (ctrl+r) at blur → focus → the read is full (`Cursor.Rewound()`), spinner on.
5. `{true,false}` after blur → flag cleared, nil Cmd; then `agentsResumeMsg` → one read.
6. `agentsResumeMsg` while blurred → nil Cmd.
7. Sessions level: blur, focus → nil Cmd, header `paused`.
8. Footer after focus has no message (`RenderFooter` holds the status line only).
9. Existing `leave_test.go` stays green (the `Leave` refactor keeps its behaviour).

**Done when:** `go test ./internal/ui/agentusageview -count=1` and
`go test ./internal/app -count=1 -run 'AgentUsage|Activity'` green; `activity_guard_test.go` untouched.

## Step 4 — containers and ports: skip the periodic fetch while blurred (S) — depends on 2; Q1; **parallel with step 3**

**Files:** `internal/ui/containers/model.go` (field), `update.go` (case `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`,
`RefreshTickMsg` branch); `internal/ui/netdiag/ports_model.go` (field `unfocused`, `handleTick`,
`setTerminalFocus(msg) (*PortsModel, tea.Cmd)`), `internal/ui/netdiag/update.go` (forward the message to
`portsModel`). Tests: `internal/ui/containers/focus_test.go`, `internal/ui/netdiag/ports_focus_test.go`.

**Behaviour:**
- containers: `RefreshTickMsg` while unfocused → `tickCmd()` only (timer kept, no
  `fetchContainers`/`fetchMetrics`). `{true,true}` → `tea.Batch(fetchContainers(), fetchMetrics())`, **no**
  `tickCmd` (the chain is still alive: one chain). `{true,false}` / `{false,_}` → flag only, nil Cmd.
- ports: `handleTick` → `if pm.paused || pm.unfocused { return pm, portsTickCmd(pm.refresh) }`.
  `{true,true}` and `!pm.paused` → `fetchPortsCmd(pm.numericAddrs)` once, no tick. The user's `paused`
  token and the status line are not touched (a separate field, not `pm.paused`).

**Tests to write first** (`testutil.FastTimers(t, &refreshInterval)` for containers; `pm.refresh` short
for ports; assert message **types** from `testutil.Msgs`, not daemon results):
1. containers blurred: `RefreshTickMsg` → the batch yields only `RefreshTickMsg`.
2. containers focus-resume: the batch yields `ContainersListMsg` and `ContainerMetricsMsg`, and no
   `RefreshTickMsg`.
3. containers entry `{true,false}` → nil Cmd.
4. ports blurred: `portsTickMsg` → only `portsTickMsg`, no `portsDataMsg`.
5. ports focus-resume → one `portsDataMsg`, no tick; with user pause on → nil Cmd, bar still shows
   `paused`.
6. netdiag routes `TerminalFocusMsg` to the ports model whatever the active tab.

**Done when:** `go test ./internal/ui/containers ./internal/ui/netdiag -count=1` and
`go test ./internal/app -count=1 -run 'Containers|Netdiag|Activity'` green.

## Step 5 — Documentation (S) — depends on 1–4 (can start with 1–2)

- `docs/architecture/app-shell.md`: new subsection "Terminal focus" after "One tick, one chain":
  the level, `wantedCadence`, why no seq bump, `TerminalFocusMsg` (edges to the view on screen, level on
  entry), H1/H2, the rule for any new periodic chain ("check the flag before I/O, keep the timer"), the
  residuals (H5, H6), the exec hand-off caveat. Update the cadence table with a "blurred → no chain" row.
- `docs/architecture/agent-usage.md` "Live updates": third header state, blur = `stopChain`, focus =
  `handleResume`, entry does not resume.
- `docs-site/docs/reference/activity-indicator.md`: the dot stops blinking and background reloads pause
  while the terminal does not have the focus; tmux needs `set -g focus-events on`; terminals without focus
  reporting behave as before.
- `docs-site/docs/explanation/app-shell.md`: one paragraph mirroring the architecture note.
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (agent-usage overview line): "paused while the terminal is not focused".
- `docs/backlog.md`: the ADR above (via `archivist`).

**Done when:** `mise run check`; `git diff origin/main -- internal/app/activity_guard_test.go` is empty.

## Step 6 — (only if Q1 = C) `app.when_unfocused: pause | run` (S) — depends on 1–4

Config key with validation and `WARN` on unknown values (like `app.motion`), `:cfg` > Appearance cycle
field (Rule 132), `docs-site/docs/reference/configuration.md`. The router's predicate becomes
`a.suspended() = a.terminalBlurred && policy == pause`; with `run`, no `TerminalFocusMsg` is sent and the
cadence ignores the blur. Tests: `run` + blur → chain renewed, views told nothing; saving the setting
while blurred (`handleConfigSaved`) applies at once (pause → run sends `{true,true}`).

## Step 7 — (only if Q2 agreed) dashboard and OCI reloads (S) — depends on 2; parallel with 3/4

Same pattern as step 4 on `HostTickMsg`, `DockerTickMsg`, dashboard `RefreshTickMsg` and
`oci_resources.RefreshTickMsg`: keep timers, skip I/O, one fetch per clock on `{true,true}`. Note the
host sparkline: a blur leaves a gap rather than a flat line — to be confirmed with ux.

## Order and parallelism

1 → 2 → (3 ∥ 4 ∥ 7) → 5; 6 after 4. Step 1 alone is a shippable PR (animation only, the ux "S"); steps
2–5 form the second PR (reloads, the ux "M").

## Risks and irreversible points

- **Terminal support (verify by hand before closing):** Windows Terminal (the user's), WSL, tmux with and
  without `focus-events`, VS Code terminal, iTerm2/Terminal.app. Unsupported → no blur → unchanged.
- **Exec hand-off (`teaexec`):** check by hand that a shell (`T`) or pager (`V`) does not print `^[[I`/`^[[O`
  when focus changes (Bubble Tea resets mode 1004 on release — confirm), and that DevDesk is not left
  blurred after the child returns (H2 covers it on the next key).
- **Visible but unfocused:** Q1. With A, the side-pane user sees `paused` and a frozen footer spinner.
- **In-flight tick after blur:** one more tick lands; handled by the level (no renewal, phase pinned on).
- **Double chain:** avoided for containers/ports by never stopping their timers; `:agent-usage` relies on
  its existing generations.
- **Timers during blur:** one 2 s wake-up per suspended view, no I/O; accepted.
- **Irreversible:** none. `ReportFocus` is a view field; removing it restores today's behaviour.

session run in another pane. With the story as written, `:agent-usage` reads nothing for as long as the
user works in the other pane, and a footer spinner of a running job freezes on one frame.
- A. As written: blur suspends blink and reloads. Simple; the `:agent-usage` "watch from the side" use case
  shows `paused (terminal not focused)` most of the time.
- B. Blur suspends the blink only; reloads keep running. Most of the battery/CPU gain is lost (reloads are
  the I/O), the visual calm stays.
- C. **(recommended)** A, plus a per-context setting `app.when_unfocused: pause | run` (default `pause`,
  the story's behaviour), editable in `:cfg` > Appearance. `run` restores today's behaviour entirely
  (blink included). It costs one config key, one `:cfg` field and one router predicate (step 6, S).
- D. Suspend reloads only after a grace period (e.g. 2 min without focus). Does not solve the side-pane
  case, adds a timer.

**Q2 — Which periodic reloads are in scope (does not block steps 1 to 5).** The story names `:agent-usage`,
container stats and ports. Others exist:

| Chain | Cadence | Cost | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| dashboard host sample (`HostTickMsg`) | 1 s | `/proc` read | include (step 7) |
| dashboard docker stats (`DockerTickMsg`) | 5 s | `docker stats`, ~2 s each — the most expensive, and the default landing view | include (step 7) |
| dashboard slow round (`RefreshTickMsg`) | ≥ 30 s | `docker system df`, `du` | include (step 7) |
| OCI resources (`oci_resources.RefreshTickMsg`) | 10 s | `docker images` | include (step 7) |
| status monitors (`status` TickMsg) | 1 s countdown + checks | HTTP/ICMP/DNS | **exclude**: monitoring is the point |
| viewer follow (`followTickMsg`) | user toggle `F` | file/log re-read | exclude: explicit user request |
| netdiag forwards tab (`forwardTickMsg`) | 2 s | in-process | exclude: no I/O |

Recommendation: ship steps 1–5 for the three named chains; step 7 (same pattern, S) for dashboard + OCI if
the user agrees.

## Hypotheses (prudent defaults, flag in the PR)

- **H1 — Unknown means focused.** The router starts focused; only a `tea.BlurMsg` suspends anything. A
  `tea.FocusMsg` with no prior blur changes nothing (no Cmd, no message to any view).
- **H2 — A key or a paste proves focus.** A `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.PasteMsg` received while blurred is
  handled as a `FocusMsg` first, then dispatched normally. Self-healing when a FocusIn is lost (tmux pane
  switch, terminal hand-off by `teaexec`, where Bubble Tea's input reader is stopped and the terminal does
  not re-report focus when mode 1004 is set again).
- **H3 — `:agent-usage` header.** `paused (terminal not focused)` whenever the agents level has an open
  aggregate and the terminal is blurred, whether or not the session was already settled (nothing is read
  while blurred, so "paused" is true either way; the reason shown is the one that resumes on focus).
- **H4 — Off-screen views are not told on the edges.** Only the view on screen has a live periodic chain
  (containers and ports chains die off screen because their ticks reach the view on screen, which drops
  them; `:agent-usage` is stopped by `Leave`). A view entering the screen is told the current state
  (level), never asked to refresh: its own `Init` does that.
- **H5 — Footer messages are not frozen.** A footer error set during the blur still expires after 3 s
  (`FooterMessage` timer). The durable trace of a failure is the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`: ⊗ on
  the row, footer detail from `DescribeRow`, `:jobs`). AC4 is about that memory; holding footer timers
  during blur would be a separate UX story.
- **H6 — Not covered, residual:** the text-input cursor blink (`bubbles/cursor`, its own chain, only while
  a field is in edit mode) and a view's own loading spinner (only while its load is in flight) keep running
  during the blur. The router does not forward raw `tea.FocusMsg`/`tea.BlurMsg` to views: `cursor.Focus()`
  on a raw focus would restart blink on cursors the view never meant to show.

## Non-functional requirements

- **CPU / battery:** blurred and idle, the router emits no `animationTickMsg`; the three named views do no
  I/O. Residual wake-ups: one 2 s timer per suspended view (containers, ports) with no I/O and no change to
  render (0 bytes written by the renderer, cf. `TestMeasureRedrawCost`).
- **Correctness:** no job is ever cancelled, paused or delayed by a blur (`jobs.Running()` unaffected);
  registry broadcasts (`ChangedMsg`, failures included) keep reaching every held view.
- **One chain:** after any Blur/Focus sequence, at most one live `animationTickMsg` chain
  (`TestTheRouterHasOneAnimationChain` unchanged and green).
- **Degradation:** a terminal that never sends `BlurMsg` behaves exactly as today (dedicated test).
- **Rules:** 110 (state changes in `Update` only), 126 (no scan on focus), 128 (no footer message on
  focus), 109 (message naming), 201 (case > 5 lines → `handle*`).
- **Guard:** `internal/app/activity_guard_test.go` is not modified. Do not add `tea.Tick` to
  `internal/ui/agentusageview` (the guard counts that package as migrated with no tick of its own); do not
  add `Frame` fields or glyph literals to `netdiag/ports_model.go`.

## Options compared (how views suspend their reloads)

| | A. Router level + views skip I/O (recommended) | B. Views stop their chains, restart on focus | C. Reuse `LeavingView.Leave()` on blur and `Init()` on focus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Router | one bool, read by the cadence; one message to the view on screen | same | calls Leave/Init |
| containers / ports | tick keeps running, the handler skips the fetch; one fetch on focus | needs a generation per chain, otherwise a focus within 2 s of the blur leaves two chains (the containers comment on `PagerExitMsg` already records that bug) | `Init()` starts a **second** `tickCmd` in containers (doubles every refresh) |
| `:agent-usage` | reuses Leave's body and `handleResume` (already generation-based) | same | works, but `Leave` also settles edits (configuration) and may refuse; `Init` reloads whole views |
| Residual wake-ups | one timer per suspended view, no I/O | none | n/a |
| Risk | low | medium (new generations in two views) | high (semantics overloaded) |

**Recommendation: A.** It is the "level, not edge" shape the router already uses for `ensureTick`, keeps
the existing chains intact, and the only new invariant is "a periodic handler checks one flag before I/O".

## ADR draft (to be archived by `archivist` in `docs/backlog.md`)

- **Context:** Bubble Tea v2 reports terminal focus (mode 1004). DevDesk animates and polls in the
  background.
- **Decision:** terminal focus is a router level (`App.terminalBlurred`, zero value = focused). The
  animation cadence reads it: blurred → no chain. Views learn it through `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`
  (to the view on screen on each edge, to a view entering the screen as a level). A periodic chain keeps
  its timer and skips its I/O while blurred; `:agent-usage` stops its chain like `Leave` and resumes like
  `handleResume`. Focus re-reads once the view on screen, never scans.
- **Consequences:** a terminal without mode 1004 is unchanged; a visible-but-unfocused DevDesk is
  paused (Q1); new periodic chains must honour the flag (documented in `app-shell.md`).

// the screen. Focused is the level; Resume is set only on the focus edge, to the
// view on screen: re-read once what was suspended (never a scan, Rule 126).
type TerminalFocusMsg struct {
	Focused bool
	Resume  bool

// internal/app/focus.go (new)

func (a *App) wantedCadence() (time.Duration, bool)        // blurred → (0, false), else cadence(...)

Recommendation: ship steps 1–5 for the three named chains; step 7 (same pattern, S) for dashboard + OCI if
the user agrees.

## Hypotheses (prudent defaults, flag in the PR)

- **H1 — Unknown means focused.** The router starts focused; only a `tea.BlurMsg` suspends anything. A
  `tea.FocusMsg` with no prior blur changes nothing (no Cmd, no message to any view).
- **H2 — A key or a paste proves focus.** A `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.PasteMsg` received while blurred is
  handled as a `FocusMsg` first, then dispatched normally. Self-healing when a FocusIn is lost (tmux pane
  switch, terminal hand-off by `teaexec`, where Bubble Tea's input reader is stopped and the terminal does
  not re-report focus when mode 1004 is set again).
- **H3 — `:agent-usage` header.** `paused (terminal not focused)` whenever the agents level has an open
  aggregate and the terminal is blurred, whether or not the session was already settled (nothing is read
  while blurred, so "paused" is true either way; the reason shown is the one that resumes on focus).
- **H4 — Off-screen views are not told on the edges.** Only the view on screen has a live periodic chain
  (containers and ports chains die off screen because their ticks reach the view on screen, which drops
  them; `:agent-usage` is stopped by `Leave`). A view entering the screen is told the current state
  (level), never asked to refresh: its own `Init` does that.
- **H5 — Footer messages are not frozen.** A footer error set during the blur still expires after 3 s
  (`FooterMessage` timer). The durable trace of a failure is the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`: ⊗ on
  the row, footer detail from `DescribeRow`, `:jobs`). AC4 is about that memory; holding footer timers
  during blur would be a separate UX story.
- **H6 — Not covered, residual:** the text-input cursor blink (`bubbles/cursor`, its own chain, only while
  a field is in edit mode) and a view's own loading spinner (only while its load is in flight) keep running
  during the blur. The router does not forward raw `tea.FocusMsg`/`tea.BlurMsg` to views: `cursor.Focus()`
  on a raw focus would restart blink on cursors the view never meant to show.

## Non-functional requirements

- **CPU / battery:** blurred and idle, the router emits no `animationTickMsg`; the three named views do no
  I/O. Residual wake-ups: one 2 s timer per suspended view (containers, ports) with no I/O and no change to
  render (0 bytes written by the renderer, cf. `TestMeasureRedrawCost`).
- **Correctness:** no job is ever cancelled, paused or delayed by a blur (`jobs.Running()` unaffected);
  registry broadcasts (`ChangedMsg`, failures included) keep reaching every held view.
- **One chain:** after any Blur/Focus sequence, at most one live `animationTickMsg` chain
  (`TestTheRouterHasOneAnimationChain` unchanged and green).
- **Degradation:** a terminal that never sends `BlurMsg` behaves exactly as today (dedicated test).
- **Rules:** 110 (state changes in `Update` only), 126 (no scan on focus), 128 (no footer message on
  focus), 109 (message naming), 201 (case > 5 lines → `handle*`).
- **Guard:** `internal/app/activity_guard_test.go` is not modified. Do not add `tea.Tick` to
  `internal/ui/agentusageview` (the guard counts that package as migrated with no tick of its own); do not
  add `Frame` fields or glyph literals to `netdiag/ports_model.go`.

## Options compared (how views suspend their reloads)

| | A. Router level + views skip I/O (recommended) | B. Views stop their chains, restart on focus | C. Reuse `LeavingView.Leave()` on blur and `Init()` on focus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Router | one bool, read by the cadence; one message to the view on screen | same | calls Leave/Init |
| containers / ports | tick keeps running, the handler skips the fetch; one fetch on focus | needs a generation per chain, otherwise a focus within 2 s of the blur leaves two chains (the containers comment on `PagerExitMsg` already records that bug) | `Init()` starts a **second** `tickCmd` in containers (doubles every refresh) |
| `:agent-usage` | reuses Leave's body and `handleResume` (already generation-based) | same | works, but `Leave` also settles edits (configuration) and may refuse; `Init` reloads whole views |
| Residual wake-ups | one timer per suspended view, no I/O | none | n/a |
| Risk | low | medium (new generations in two views) | high (semantics overloaded) |

**Recommendation: A.** It is the "level, not edge" shape the router already uses for `ensureTick`, keeps
the existing chains intact, and the only new invariant is "a periodic handler checks one flag before I/O".

## ADR draft (to be archived by `archivist` in `docs/backlog.md`)

- **Context:** Bubble Tea v2 reports terminal focus (mode 1004). DevDesk animates and polls in the
  background.
- **Decision:** terminal focus is a router level (`App.terminalBlurred`, zero value = focused). The
  animation cadence reads it: blurred → no chain. Views learn it through `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`
  (to the view on screen on each edge, to a view entering the screen as a level). A periodic chain keeps
  its timer and skips its I/O while blurred; `:agent-usage` stops its chain like `Leave` and resumes like
  `handleResume`. Focus re-reads once the view on screen, never scans.
- **Consequences:** a terminal without mode 1004 is unchanged; a visible-but-unfocused DevDesk is
  paused (Q1); new periodic chains must honour the flag (documented in `app-shell.md`).

## Interfaces (shared by the steps)

```go
// internal/shared/focus.go (new)
// TerminalFocusMsg tells a view whether the terminal has the focus. The router
// sends it to the view on screen when the focus changes, and to a view entering
// the screen. Focused is the level; Resume is set only on the focus edge, to the
// view on screen: re-read once what was suspended (never a scan, Rule 126).
type TerminalFocusMsg struct {
	Focused bool
	Resume  bool
}

// internal/app/focus.go (new)

func (a *App) wantedCadence() (time.Duration, bool)        // blurred → (0, false), else cadence(...)
```

`App` gains `terminalBlurred bool` (zero value = focused, H1). `cadence()` keeps its signature (existing
tests untouched); `ensureTick` and `handleAnimationTick` call `a.wantedCadence()` instead.

1 → 2 → (3 ∥ 4 ∥ 7) → 5; 6 after 4. Step 1 alone is a shippable PR (animation only, the ux "S"); steps

`docs/architecture/app-shell.md` ("The broadcast, and the animation tick", "One tick, one chain"),

**Q1 — A terminal that is visible but not focused (blocks steps 3 and 4, not 1 and 2).**

session run in another pane. With the story as written, `:agent-usage` reads nothing for as long as the
user works in the other pane, and a footer spinner of a running job freezes on one frame.
- A. As written: blur suspends blink and reloads. Simple; the `:agent-usage` "watch from the side" use case

- B. Blur suspends the blink only; reloads keep running. Most of the battery/CPU gain is lost (reloads are
  the I/O), the visual calm stays.

| viewer follow (`followTickMsg`) | user toggle `F` | file/log re-read | exclude: explicit user request |

  on a raw focus would restart blink on cursors the view never meant to show.

## Non-functional requirements

- **CPU / battery:** blurred and idle, the router emits no `animationTickMsg`; the three named views do no
  I/O. Residual wake-ups: one 2 s timer per suspended view (containers, ports) with no I/O and no change to
  render (0 bytes written by the renderer, cf. `TestMeasureRedrawCost`).
- **Correctness:** no job is ever cancelled, paused or delayed by a blur (`jobs.Running()` unaffected);
  registry broadcasts (`ChangedMsg`, failures included) keep reaching every held view.
- **One chain:** after any Blur/Focus sequence, at most one live `animationTickMsg` chain
  (`TestTheRouterHasOneAnimationChain` unchanged and green).
- **Degradation:** a terminal that never sends `BlurMsg` behaves exactly as today (dedicated test).
- **Rules:** 110 (state changes in `Update` only), 126 (no scan on focus), 128 (no footer message on
  focus), 109 (message naming), 201 (case > 5 lines → `handle*`).
- **Guard:** `internal/app/activity_guard_test.go` is not modified. Do not add `tea.Tick` to
  `internal/ui/agentusageview` (the guard counts that package as migrated with no tick of its own); do not
  add `Frame` fields or glyph literals to `netdiag/ports_model.go`.

## Options compared (how views suspend their reloads)

| | A. Router level + views skip I/O (recommended) | B. Views stop their chains, restart on focus | C. Reuse `LeavingView.Leave()` on blur and `Init()` on focus |
|---|---|---|---|
| Router | one bool, read by the cadence; one message to the view on screen | same | calls Leave/Init |
| containers / ports | tick keeps running, the handler skips the fetch; one fetch on focus | needs a generation per chain, otherwise a focus within 2 s of the blur leaves two chains (the containers comment on `PagerExitMsg` already records that bug) | `Init()` starts a **second** `tickCmd` in containers (doubles every refresh) |
| `:agent-usage` | reuses Leave's body and `handleResume` (already generation-based) | same | works, but `Leave` also settles edits (configuration) and may refuse; `Init` reloads whole views |
| Residual wake-ups | one timer per suspended view, no I/O | none | n/a |
| Risk | low | medium (new generations in two views) | high (semantics overloaded) |

**Recommendation: A.** It is the "level, not edge" shape the router already uses for `ensureTick`, keeps
the existing chains intact, and the only new invariant is "a periodic handler checks one flag before I/O".

## ADR draft (to be archived by `archivist` in `docs/backlog.md`)

- **Context:** Bubble Tea v2 reports terminal focus (mode 1004). DevDesk animates and polls in the
  background.
- **Decision:** terminal focus is a router level (`App.terminalBlurred`, zero value = focused). The
  animation cadence reads it: blurred → no chain. Views learn it through `shared.TerminalFocusMsg`
  (to the view on screen on each edge, to a view entering the screen as a level). A periodic chain keeps
  its timer and skips its I/O while blurred; `:agent-usage` stops its chain like `Leave` and resumes like
  `handleResume`. Focus re-reads once the view on screen, never scans.
- **Consequences:** a terminal without mode 1004 is unchanged; a visible-but-unfocused DevDesk is
  paused (Q1); new periodic chains must honour the flag (documented in `app-shell.md`).

// the screen. Focused is the level; Resume is set only on the focus edge, to the
// view on screen: re-read once what was suspended (never a scan, Rule 126).
type TerminalFocusMsg struct {
	Focused bool
	Resume  bool
}

// internal/app/focus.go (new)
func (a *App) handleTerminalBlur() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)
func (a *App) handleTerminalFocus() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)
func (a *App) sendFocusTo(target command.ViewType) tea.Cmd // level, Resume=false
func (a *App) wantedCadence() (time.Duration, bool)        // blurred → (0, false), else cadence(...)
```

`App` gains `terminalBlurred bool` (zero value = focused, H1). `cadence()` keeps its signature (existing
tests untouched); `ensureTick` and `handleAnimationTick` call `a.wantedCadence()` instead.

1 → 2 → (3 ∥ 4 ∥ 7) → 5; 6 after 4. Step 1 alone is a shippable PR (animation only, the ux "S"); steps
2–5 form the second PR (reloads, the ux "M").

## Risks and irreversible points

- **Terminal support (verify by hand before closing):** Windows Terminal (the user's), WSL, tmux with and
  without `focus-events`, VS Code terminal, iTerm2/Terminal.app. Unsupported → no blur → unchanged.
- **Exec hand-off (`teaexec`):** check by hand that a shell (`T`) or pager (`V`) does not print `^[[I`/`^[[O`

Il y a un brouillon d'ADR dans le plan, à archiver par `archivist`.

1. **Animation seule, effort S, livrable comme une PR à part.** `App.View()` pose `ReportFocus`. Sur `BlurMsg`, on pose le booléen et rien d'autre : le tick déjà en route n'est pas renouvelé et la phase reste sur « on ». Sur `FocusMsg`, `ensureTick` relance une seule chaîne ; un `FocusMsg` sans blur préalable ne fait rien. `cadence()` garde sa signature (nouvelle méthode `wantedCadence()`), donc `TestTheRouterHasOneAnimationChain` ne change pas. Dix tests sont listés, dont les critères 3, 4, 5 et 6, un test de dégradation « jamais de BlurMsg » et un test `-race` sur un vrai `tea.Program`.
2. **Message `shared.TerminalFocusMsg{Focused, Resume}`, effort S.** Il part vers la vue à l'écran à chaque changement de focus. Une vue qui entre à l'écran (`enterView`, `reinitializeViews`) reçoit l'état courant, sans `Resume`. Pas d'`Init`, pas de scan (Rule 126), pas de footer (Rule 128).

4. **containers et ports, effort S, en parallèle de l'étape 3.** Le tick continue sans lecture ; au retour du focus, une seule lecture, sans nouveau tick. La pause choisie par l'utilisateur dans ports reste indépendante.
5. **Documentation.** `app-shell.md`, `agent-usage.md`, `docs-site` (`reference/activity-indicator.md` avec tmux `set -g focus-events on`, `explanation/app-shell.md`), la ligne de `.claude/CLAUDE.md` et `docs/backlog.md`.
6. **Seulement si Q1 = C** : le réglage `app.when_unfocused`.
7. **Seulement si Q2 est accepté** : dashboard et OCI.

- Une touche ou un collage reçus pendant le blur valent un retour du focus. Ça corrige un FocusIn perdu, par exemple sous tmux ou après la main rendue par `teaexec`.
- Un message d'erreur du footer expire toujours au bout de 3 s pendant le blur. La trace durable reste la mémoire d'échec (`jobs.FailureKey`, ⊗ sur la ligne, `:jobs`), ce que vise le critère 4.
- Deux animations continuent pendant le blur : le clignotement du curseur des champs texte (bubbles) et le spinner de chargement propre à une vue. Le routeur ne transmet pas les `FocusMsg`/`BlurMsg` bruts aux vues.

## Risques

- **Prise en charge par terminal, à vérifier à la main** : Windows Terminal, WSL, tmux avec et sans `focus-events`, VS Code. Un terminal sans support reste au comportement actuel.
- **Main rendue à un processus enfant (`T`, `V`)** : vérifier qu'aucun `^[[I`/`^[[O` n'apparaît dans le shell ou le pager.
- **Réveils pendant le blur** : il reste un timer de 2 s par vue suspendue, sans lecture. Je l'accepte.
- **Le cas Q1** ci-dessus.
- **Rien d'irréversible** : retirer `ReportFocus` rétablit le comportement actuel.

- **C (recommandée)** : A, plus un réglage par contexte `app.when_unfocused: pause | run`, `pause` par défaut, modifiable dans `:cfg` (étape 6, effort S).
- D : suspendre après un délai de grâce ; ça ne règle pas le cas des volets.

**Q2 — Périmètre des relectures (ne bloque pas les étapes 1 à 5).** Je propose d'ajouter les rafraîchissements du dashboard (échantillon hôte 1 s, `docker stats` toutes les 5 s, c'est le plus coûteux et c'est la vue d'accueil) et le rafraîchissement OCI de 10 s (étape 7, effort S). Je propose de laisser hors périmètre les moniteurs `:status` (ils servent justement à surveiller), le suivi `F` du viewer (demandé explicitement par l'utilisateur) et l'onglet forwards (aucune entrée-sortie).

## Le plan

Option retenue : le routeur tient un seul booléen, `terminalBlurred`, qui vaut « focus » par défaut. La cadence d'animation le lit, et chaque vue saute ses lectures périodiques tant qu'il est vrai, sans arrêter sa chaîne de tick. J'ai écarté deux options :
- arrêter puis relancer les chaînes : il faudrait des générations, sinon on risque une double chaîne dans containers ;
- réutiliser `Leave`/`Init` : `Init` de containers relance un second tick, ce qui doublerait chaque rafraîchissement.

Il y a un brouillon d'ADR dans le plan, à archiver par `archivist`.

1. **Animation seule, effort S, livrable comme une PR à part.** `App.View()` pose `ReportFocus`. Sur `BlurMsg`, on pose le booléen et rien d'autre : le tick déjà en route n'est pas renouvelé et la phase reste sur « on ». Sur `FocusMsg`, `ensureTick` relance une seule chaîne ; un `FocusMsg` sans blur préalable ne fait rien. `cadence()` garde sa signature (nouvelle méthode `wantedCadence()`), donc `TestTheRouterHasOneAnimationChain` ne change pas. Dix tests sont listés, dont les critères 3, 4, 5 et 6, un test de dégradation « jamais de BlurMsg » et un test `-race` sur un vrai `tea.Program`.
2. **Message `shared.TerminalFocusMsg{Focused, Resume}`, effort S.** Il part vers la vue à l'écran à chaque changement de focus. Une vue qui entre à l'écran (`enterView`, `reinitializeViews`) reçoit l'état courant, sans `Resume`. Pas d'`Init`, pas de scan (Rule 126), pas de footer (Rule 128).
3. **`:agent-usage`, effort M-.** Le blur réutilise le corps de `Leave` (extrait dans `stopChain()`), le retour du focus appelle `handleResume`. L'en-tête affiche « paused (terminal not focused) ». Aucun `tea.Tick` n'est ajouté au package, donc `activity_guard_test.go` reste intact.
4. **containers et ports, effort S, en parallèle de l'étape 3.** Le tick continue sans lecture ; au retour du focus, une seule lecture, sans nouveau tick. La pause choisie par l'utilisateur dans ports reste indépendante.
5. **Documentation.** `app-shell.md`, `agent-usage.md`, `docs-site` (`reference/activity-indicator.md` avec tmux `set -g focus-events on`, `explanation/app-shell.md`), la ligne de `.claude/CLAUDE.md` et `docs/backlog.md`.
6. **Seulement si Q1 = C** : le réglage `app.when_unfocused`.
7. **Seulement si Q2 est accepté** : dashboard et OCI.

Ordre : 1 → 2 → (3 ∥ 4 ∥ 7) → 5, et 6 après 4. Chaque étape donne sa commande de tests ciblés (`go test ./internal/app -run 'Focus|Blur|…'`, `go test ./internal/ui/agentusageview`, etc.).

## Hypothèses à signaler dans la PR

- Une touche ou un collage reçus pendant le blur valent un retour du focus. Ça corrige un FocusIn perdu, par exemple sous tmux ou après la main rendue par `teaexec`.
- Un message d'erreur du footer expire toujours au bout de 3 s pendant le blur. La trace durable reste la mémoire d'échec (`jobs.FailureKey`, ⊗ sur la ligne, `:jobs`), ce que vise le critère 4.
- Deux animations continuent pendant le blur : le clignotement du curseur des champs texte (bubbles) et le spinner de chargement propre à une vue. Le routeur ne transmet pas les `FocusMsg`/`BlurMsg` bruts aux vues.

## Risques

- **Prise en charge par terminal, à vérifier à la main** : Windows Terminal, WSL, tmux avec et sans `focus-events`, VS Code. Un terminal sans support reste au comportement actuel.
- **Main rendue à un processus enfant (`T`, `V`)** : vérifier qu'aucun `^[[I`/`^[[O` n'apparaît dans le shell ou le pager.
- **Réveils pendant le blur** : il reste un timer de 2 s par vue suspendue, sans lecture. Je l'accepte.
- **Le cas Q1** ci-dessus.
- **Rien d'irréversible** : retirer `ReportFocus` rétablit le comportement actuel.
